requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long
requirements.summary: libpam-pwquality installed, minlen=12 added to /etc/security/pwquality.conf, and a live passwd attempt by an unprivileged user with a password under 12 characters was rejected with an explicit 'password is shorter than 12 characters' message both before and after the node restart, while a compliant longer password was accepted.

requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must use at least three different character classes
requirements.summary: minclass=3 added to pwquality.conf; a live passwd attempt with a lowercase-only password was rejected with 'password contains less than 3 character classes', while a 4-class password was accepted, both before and after the restart.

requirements.requirement: Policy must actually be enforced via PAM on new password changes (not just present in a config file)
requirements.summary: grep confirms pam_pwquality.so is wired into /etc/pam.d/common-password (via requisite), and functional passwd tests as an unprivileged user demonstrate the policy is enforced end-to-end, not merely configured.

overall_summary: The executor correctly installed libpam-pwquality and set minlen=12/minclass=3 in pwquality.conf on node1, and directly demonstrated enforcement via live passwd attempts as an unprivileged user: passwords under 12 characters were rejected, passwords with fewer than 3 character classes were rejected, and a compliant password was accepted. This was verified both before and after a full node restart (boot_id changed from f9bf293d... to 902575df..., matching the fixed global snapshots), confirming the policy persists across reboot. Temporary test users were cleaned up and no unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found; the environment returned to a clean state.
limitations: The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was applied here as a single-node restart; boot-identity, acknowledgement, and post-restart functional re-verification are all present and consistent with the fixed global snapshots, but there was no separate cluster/data-recovery check since this is a single-node, non-clustered task.

Password contents were redacted in captured stdout ('[REDACTED]'), so exact test password strings could not be independently re-derived, but the pam_pwquality diagnostic messages and exit codes provide sufficient behavioral evidence of enforcement.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map cleanly to the task: package install, config append, and two rounds of temporary test-user creation/passwd-testing/deletion (pre- and post-restart) to validate the policy live. Both test users (pwtestuser, pwverify) were deleted after use; userdel returned rc=1 only due to a harmless 'mail spool not found' warning, with 'id' confirming the users no longer exist. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary mutations were found — after_executor snapshot shows only expected reboot-driven differences (new boot_id, new /tmp systemd-private dirs, listening sockets re-bound to a new resolver pid), all matching a normal reboot, not executor residue. The restart itself (shutdown -r now) was a required action for the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol.
